hero.headline: Indian River County responds to Vero Beach condo owner concerns over waste management fee spike
hero.teaser: A Vero Beach condo owner saw his monthly waste management fees jump from $11 to $21 under a new contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025.
hero.body:
Thomas Clark spoke with WPTV Anchor Mike Trim during a Let's Hear It event about concerns regarding his monthly condo association bill. His waste management fees had jumped nearly double in Vero Beach. WPTV brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services, which explained during a video conference meeting that the increase stems from a new contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025. The new contract raised average condo association waste management fees from $11 to $21, a roughly 93% increase.

Clark expressed his frustration with the situation. He told Trim that he is not really happy with the increase, to be honest. He said he understands that if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end. Clark suggested that county officials should maybe look at something to help residents out with the financial impact.

However, county officials say condo owners are getting additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during 2024 hearings. They indicated that residents had the opportunity to participate in the decision-making process before the contract was finalized.

Mehta said if Clark or his homeowners association wanted to invite county officials to a meeting, they would be happy to send someone to go over the process in more detail. He stated that it is certainly something he is available for and that his team is available to provide that information. For more information, residents can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings through county resources. Current recycling and garbage schedules are also available through the county.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce plans overhaul of waterfront property management after multiple lawsuits
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from plaintiff Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling o.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from plaintiff Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of the historic Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement wasn't practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. Keene told WPTV the city will continue the litigation and he wants transparency, not money. Broderick said the city has an obligation to defend the case and feels the lawsuit doesn't have any merit.

The Little Jim Bait & Tackle case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute WPTV has reported on and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, King's Landing developer Dale Matteson threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, Fisherman's Wharf developer Chris Shelli filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it didn't own. In 2025, the city abruptly canceled the Little Jim's bidding process amid public outcry, prompting Keene's lawsuit and leaving developers Luigi and Drita Lucaj frustrated. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant. Broderick acknowledged the controversies in an interview with WPTV and said the city's waterfront properties are not being managed. The city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties.

cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from plaintiff Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of the historic Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement was not practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. Broderick told WPTV he also feels the lawsuit does not have any merit, though he acknowledged some of the controversies mentioned in the suit, which allege a broader pattern of defective administration of city waterfront properties.

The Little Jim Bait & Tackle case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute WPTV has reported on, and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, the developer of King's Landing threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, the developer of Fisherman's Wharf, Chris Shelli, filed suit against the city after state records showed the city promised property it did not own. Then in 2025, Little Jim's land lease expired and the city sought bids to take over the property. Amid public outcry, the city abruptly canceled the process, prompting Keene's lawsuit and leaving at least two developers frustrated. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant.

When asked how he would respond to allegations that this is an example of a pattern of mismanaging waterfront properties, Broderick told WPTV he would not say the properties are managed poorly but rather that they are not being managed, an issue he takes very seriously. The commissioner said the city is taking a top down, bottom up approach to look at the entirety of the portfolio of Fort Pierce properties and fix issues one asset at a time. Broderick said the city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties with the goal of preventing these problems from happening again.

Both sides say they are open to negotiating. Keene told WPTV he will continue the litigation and the fight, adding that he wants transparency, not money, and is willing to revise his offer. Broderick says he will consider any feasible settlement that keeps the case out of court, though the city has an obligation to defend itself against the lawsuit.

cards.headline: Vero Beach condo waste management fees nearly double under new Indian River County contract
cards.body:
Indian River County officials met with WPTV to address concerns from Vero Beach condo owners facing a significant increase in waste management fees. Thomas Clark raised the issue during a WPTV Let's Hear It event, telling anchor Mike Trim that his monthly condo association waste management fees had jumped from $11 to $21, representing a roughly 93% increase.

The fee increase results from a new contract with Waste Management that took effect in October 2025. WPTV brought Clark's concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. County officials confirmed that the new contract raised average condo association waste management fees from the previous $11 monthly rate to the current $21 rate. Clark expressed his dissatisfaction with the increase, telling Trim he was not happy about it. He suggested that if the county made a mistake, officials should consider helping residents. "I understand that if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end, you would think," Clark said. "Maybe look at something to help us out."

County officials explained that condo owners are receiving additional services under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District said residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during hearings held in 2024. They encouraged residents to participate in these public meetings to stay informed about changes that affect their fees and services.

Mehta offered to provide more detailed explanations of the contract process to concerned residents. "If this gentleman wanted to invite us or his HOA wanted to invite us to a meeting, we're happy to send someone to go over this process in more detail," Mehta said. "It's certainly something I'm available for — my team is available to provide that." Residents seeking more information can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings through the county website. Current recycling and garbage schedules are also available on the county's online resources.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County to offer free rip current safety training at three pool sessions this summer
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County residents and visitors will have the chance to learn life-saving skills through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools using a new rip current simulation machine.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. The first is July 19 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool, with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The second is July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event, with no registration required and first-come, first-served. The third is August 16 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool, with registration required and limited to 50 participants.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Park restroom and concession building rebuild pushed to late 2027
cards.body:
Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The site is currently an empty plot of land, leaving beachgoers with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach. Gonda Ghebert, who contacted the station about the issue, says the situation has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Beachgoers also miss the cafe that was part of the destroyed facility. Julie Goings says she went to the beach because of the nice, clean facility and showers, and enjoyed being able to get a snack or drink after coming off the deck. Sam Elliott says the only thing really missing is concessions and food availability.

Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director, says the permitting process takes time because the building sits on a protected dune and requires approval from the Department of Environmental Protection. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80% complete. The building will be about 15 feet in elevation with 100 seats and 33 at the bar. Abbate says they want to do it right, and if they design it properly, they will have fewer issues when they get through construction and it will be a much smoother process. He believes the cafe will be worth the wait.

The county expects final funding approval in September. Construction is planned to start in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county has no plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities in the meantime. Those who use the beach say they are anxiously awaiting construction of the new facility.

Elliott says he is hoping it moves real fast. Goings says she wants the bathrooms up and running and it would be nice to have another little convenient spot. The prolonged timeline means beachgoers will continue dealing with limited restroom facilities for at least another two years while the county works through the permitting and construction process for the replacement building.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website back online after temporary redirection issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday morning, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online around 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online by about 1:30 p.m. Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon saying the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider. Miller assured the public that at no time was personal or confidential information compromised or at risk. The clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website.

Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo said he immediately ordered the site turned off and started an investigation. The clerk's office communications team said this wasn't a hack because there wasn't any personal information compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available, with only the main page affected. The office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again. Clavijo said as soon as the office identifies the exact issue, there will be a tremendous remediation.

hero.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 LA Olympics
hero.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
hero.body:
The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said. The move was expected since the committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem, saying that decision will come at an appropriate time. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening October 31. The IOC said Russian athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to stunning 3-2 comeback over Egypt to reach World Cup quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Messi scored his record-extending 21st World Cup goal in the 83rd minute as Argentina rallied from a 2-0 deficit with 11 minutes remaining in regulation.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to a 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play. The defending champions will face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri.

Messi leveled the score at 2-2 in the 83rd minute with his record-extending 21st World Cup goal. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute, and Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, also missed a penalty kick in the first half when his shot was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir, and later hit the post when the score was 1-0.

Egypt had taken a surprising 2-0 lead on goals from Yasser Ibrahim in the 15th minute and Mostafa Zico in the 67th minute. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said after the match, "I'm so emotional. What a group of players, brother."

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in round of 16
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. While the U.S. was boosted by the presence of star forward Folarin Balogun, whose one-game red-card suspension was controversially lifted by FIFA, American defenders were at fault in a pair of first-half goals and goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third early in the second half. Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 in the 31st minute with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff when De Ketelaere outjumped Tim Ream and headed the ball past Freese in the 33rd minute. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt and was replaced seven minutes later.

Belgium built a two-goal lead when Freese hesitated with a touch after chesting a long ball, and Hans Vanaken one-timed a shot from 35 yards that deflected in off Ream in the 57th minute. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time after Belgium stripped the ball from Chris Richards. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed in its quest to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930. A crowd of 66,925 at Lumen Field watched as coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. Belgium extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games and plays 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Roll Past Jupiter 11-2 in Series Opener
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets opened their road series against the Jupiter Hammerheads with an 11-2 rout Tuesday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, leading from the first pitch to the las
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets opened their road series against the Jupiter Hammerheads with an 11-2 rout Tuesday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, leading from the first pitch to the last.

Leadoff hitter Antonio Jimenez set the tone immediately, homering on the very first pitch of the game from Jupiter starter Jonas Uzcategui. Jimenez finished the night 4 for 6 with the home run, two doubles, four runs scored and two stolen bases. He came a triple short of the cycle, striking out and hitting into a fielder's choice in his final two at-bats.

Four St. Lucie pitchers held the Hammerheads to just two hits. Starter Jose Lopez, making his team debut, worked four solid innings, allowing one hit and two runs with four walks and four strikeouts. Relievers Zack Mack, Miguel Mejias and Elwis Mijares combined for five innings of one-hit relief. Mack earned the win.

The Mets built a 3-0 lead through two innings before Jupiter answered with two runs and put the tying run on third base in the fourth. Lopez escaped the jam by getting Edgardo De Leon to pop out, preserving a 3-2 lead.

St. Lucie broke the game open with four runs in the sixth. Branny De Oleo drove in a run with a single, Jimenez scored on a wild pitch, and AJ Salgado added a two-run single to push the lead to 7-2.

The Mets tacked on two unearned runs in the eighth on a Jupiter error and another run-scoring wild pitch, then closed the scoring in the ninth on a De Oleo RBI single and yet another wild pitch that brought Jimenez home.

De Oleo went 2 for 5 with three RBI and Salgado added two hits and two RBI. Julio Zayas drew four walks, while Jeremy Rodriguez walked twice and scored two runs.

The win improved St. Lucie to 8-2 at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium this season and marked its third straight victory over Jupiter. The Mets (4-10, 37-43) and Hammerheads (5-11, 42-40) continue their series Wednesday, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach in November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The festival announcement was made Monday.

The annual event brings seafood vendors and attractions to the Treasure Coast community. The festival has become a recurring event in Vero Beach over nearly two decades.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is organizing the November festival. The company has managed the event for previous years.

Further scheduling details about the November festival dates will be released by the event organizers.

hero.headline: Leon County judge sets hearing dates for Fishback ballot challenge in Florida governor's race
hero.body:
A Leon County judge has scheduled two days of hearings later this month to decide whether Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback meets Florida's residency requirements to remain on the ballot. Judge David Frank set the matter for July 21 and 22 during a Tuesday scheduling hearing, warning attorneys there is an extreme shortage of time with the Aug. 18 primary approaching. Frank also noted it is likely already too late to stop ballots from being printed, saying there would need to be an injunction to the Department of State telling supervisors of elections not to count votes for Fishback and to post a notice.

Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's rivals in the GOP primary, filed the lawsuit arguing Fishback does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement to run for governor. The complaint points to records tied to Fishback's voter registration and residency in Washington, D.C. Fishback's attorney, former state representative Anthony Sabatini, told the judge the case turns on more than paperwork, arguing Fishback's intent will be central to determining residency. Sabatini said the defense wants time to present witnesses and documents. Witness and exhibit lists are due five days before the July 21 hearing.

The courtroom fight comes just days after the issue spilled onto the debate stage. During last week's GOP primary debate, Fishback, Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner appeared together. Frontrunner Byron Donalds skipped the event but still loomed large over the debate, with his rivals repeatedly invoking him and his position in the race. Fishback pressed Collins directly over the lawsuit, getting the state's lieutenant governor to note his Florida roots. "Case closed. Drop the lawsuit," Fishback said during the debate. He later accused Collins of trying to steal the election with Byron Donalds. Collins pushed back, saying the challenge belongs in court. "That is a matter for the court," Collins said. "I actually respect the judicial system."

For now, Fishback remains on the ballot, but the case adds uncertainty to the primary calendar at a time when election officials are already preparing ballots and candidates are running out of time to shift the race. Even if Fishback is removed, the broader GOP contest may still revolve around Donalds, who has maintained a commanding position in the primary through polling, fundraising and endorsements. Axios reported Tuesday that Donalds continues to tower over the field as the Aug. 18 primary approaches.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach Park restroom and concession rebuild delayed until late 2027
hero.body:
Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The site is currently an empty plot of land, leaving beachgoers with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach. The limited facilities have become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season, according to beachgoer Gonda Ghebert, who reached out to WPTV.

Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director, says the permitting process takes time because the facility sits on a protected dune and must go through the Department of Environmental Protection. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80 percent complete. The facility will stand at about 15 feet in elevation with 100 seats and 33 at the bar. Abbate says the county wants to design it properly so there will be fewer issues during construction and a much smoother process overall.

The county says final funding is expected to be approved in September. They hope to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county does not have any plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities. However, Abbate says the cafe will be worth the wait.

Those who frequent the beach say they miss the cafe and are anxiously awaiting its construction. Julie Goings said the reason she went there was because they had a nice, clean facility, showers, and it was just nice coming off the deck being able to get a snack or drink. Sam Elliott said the only thing that is really missing is concessions and food availability. Goings said she wants the bathrooms up and running and it would be nice to have another little convenient spot. Elliott said he is hoping the project moves real fast.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at local pools this summer
hero.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can learn life-saving skills this summer through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques.

Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. Rip currents are powerful channels of water that flow away from shore, capable of quickly pulling swimmers away from the beach. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States.

Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle. The hands-on training aims to build swimmer confidence and prepare participants for real ocean conditions before they head to area beaches.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. The first session takes place July 19 from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool, with registration required and participation limited to 50 people. The second session is scheduled for July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event, with no registration required and available on a first-come, first-served basis. The final session will be held August 16 from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool, with registration required and limited to 50 participants. For more information about the rip current safety demonstrations, residents can contact St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man, 28, dies after weekend shooting on South 14th Street
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce early Sunday morning, according to police.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend, according to police. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street. Officers arrived at the scene and found two people with apparent gunshot wounds. The 28-year-old man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a local hospital but died from his injuries on Tuesday.

Officers also found a 28-year-old woman with injuries to her hand from the shooting, but her injuries were described as not life-threatening. Police said a preliminary investigation indicated that the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation in the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As they arrived home, police said a man believed to be involved in the previous altercation approached and opened fire before fleeing the area. Police said this investigation remains active and ongoing. The names of the victims have not been released. Anyone with information in the case is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man, 66, killed in shooting on Essex Drive; suspect in custody
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified the victim in Tuesday afternoon's shooting on Essex Drive as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the victim in Tuesday afternoon's shooting on Essex Drive as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Deputies responded around 3:30 p.m. to a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned an adult man had shot another adult man with a rifle.

Deputies took the suspect into custody and began providing emergency medical care to Barnes until St. Lucie County Fire District personnel arrived. Barnes was then taken to a local hospital, where he died. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division are continuing to process evidence, conduct interviews, and work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The suspect remains in custody. Investigators say there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce creates new real estate position to manage waterfront properties after multiple lawsuits
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from plaintiff Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of the historic Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement wasn't practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. Broderick said the city still has to defend the lawsuit and feels it doesn't have any merit.

The Little Jim Bait & Tackle case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, developer Dale Matteson of King's Landing threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, Fisherman's Wharf developer Chris Shelli filed suit against the city after state records showed the city promised property it didn't own. In 2025, Little Jim's land lease expired and the city sought bids to take over the property. Amid public outcry, the city abruptly canceled the process, prompting Keene's lawsuit and leaving developers Luigi and Drita Lucaj frustrated. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant. Broderick said the city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties. Both sides say they are open to negotiating.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website down for hours Tuesday due to third-party issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site. The website was back online by about 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the website outage that redirected visitors to another site for hours. The website was back online by about 1:30 p.m. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider. She assured the public that at no time was personal or confidential information compromised or at risk. The clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website.

Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said the office received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo said he turned it off as soon as he identified the issue and started an investigation. The clerk's office communications team said this was not a hack because there was not any personal information compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available, with only the main page affected. The office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again, and Clavijo said there will be a tremendous remediation as soon as the office identifies the exact issue.

hero.headline: Vero Beach condo waste management fees nearly double under new Indian River County contract
hero.body:
Indian River County officials met with WPTV to address concerns from Vero Beach condo owners facing a significant increase in waste management fees. Thomas Clark raised the issue during a WPTV Let's Hear It event, telling anchor Mike Trim that his monthly condo association waste management fees had jumped from $11 to $21, representing a roughly 93% increase.

The fee increase results from a new contract with Waste Management that took effect in October 2025. WPTV brought Clark's concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. County officials confirmed that the new contract raised average condo association waste management fees from the previous $11 monthly rate to the current $21 rate. Clark expressed his dissatisfaction with the increase, telling Trim he was not happy about it. He suggested that if the county made a mistake, officials should consider helping residents. "I understand that if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end, you would think," Clark said. "Maybe look at something to help us out."

County officials explained that condo owners are receiving additional services under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District said residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during hearings held in 2024. They encouraged residents to participate in these public meetings to stay informed about changes that affect their fees and services.

Mehta offered to provide more detailed explanations of the contract process to concerned residents. "If this gentleman wanted to invite us or his HOA wanted to invite us to a meeting, we're happy to send someone to go over this process in more detail," Mehta said. "It's certainly something I'm available for — my team is available to provide that." Residents seeking more information can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings through the county website. Current recycling and garbage schedules are also available on the county's online resources.
